recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow source fix to the active Search page and resolves the remaining implementer-visible inaccuracies in the examples without reopening the already-decided related FHIR-39318 work.
issue_request: FHIR-39316 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I clarification for R5 asking for examples of invoking a named query with _query=current-high-risk, including GET and POST forms, ward and birthdate examples, and a variation where a non-_query parameter appears before _query.
initial_application: Git commits 7399925f104938ec96ee55b81f92a2e6e5810fcc and 8379376575fc965f7d3d6bb4d228804f296e2a87 added the current-high-risk OperationDefinition and request table to source/search.html. The current source retained the example section but still had a mistyped GET birthdate, showed _query first in every request, and used the obsolete output parameter name return in the inline OperationDefinition.
additional_context: source/search.html is in build scope because publish.ini lists search.html and source/hierarchy.xml places it under the RESTful API page. The originating Zulip thread asked exactly how named queries are invoked and whether Patient?param1=foo&_query=myquery is valid. Related FHIR-39318 later clarified unordered _query handling and the single result Bundle output parameter; an FHIR-39318 reconciliation commit already exists on the combined branch, so no duplicate related commit was published.
reconciliation: Changed the inline OperationDefinition output parameter from return to result, fixed the malformed ge1970-01-1 GET example, clarified the birthdate example text, and changed the final GET and POST examples so birthdate appears before _query.
source_changes: source/search.html: corrected the inline current-high-risk OperationDefinition output parameter name from return to result.
source/search.html: fixed the malformed GET birthdate value ge1970-01-1 to ge1970-01-01.
source/search.html: changed the final GET and POST invocation examples to place birthdate before _query and updated the description to state that this is intentional.
